description: 2MASS Redshift Survey galaxies (Ks<=11.75, |b|>=5 deg, >=8 deg towards the bulge) as 3D points in comoving space for the cosmic-web view.

fields.name: zMpc
fields.description: comoving z: towards Dec=+90 (ICRS north pole)

fields.name: redshift
fields.description: CMB-frame redshift z_cmb used for the distance (see redshiftFrame)

fields.name: kMag
fields.description: 2MRS Kcmag: extinction-corrected 2MASS Ks isophotal magnitude (K=20 mag/arcsec^2 isophote)

nullHandling: No nulls: galaxies without a redshift (or with z_cmb<=0) are excluded and counted in selection.
order: Randomly shuffled (mulberry32 seed 20121226); any prefix of N records is a uniform random subsample. Row i corresponds to row i of cosmicweb-2mrs-meta.json.

coordinateFrame.axes: ICRS (J2000) equatorial Cartesian; x=(cos dec cos ra), y=(cos dec sin ra), z=(sin dec) times comoving distance
coordinateFrame.origin: observer (solar-system barycentre); the Milky Way is at the origin
coordinateFrame.positionsAre: redshift-space (derived): peculiar velocities are not removed; clusters appear elongated along the line of sight (Fingers of God), and very nearby galaxies (z_cmb<0.003, D<~13 Mpc) have large relative distance errors.

redshiftFrame.conversion: 1+z_cmb = (1+z_hel) * gamma * (1 + beta*cos(theta)); beta = v/c, theta = angle to CMB dipole apex

cmbDipole.ref: Planck Collaboration 2020, A&A 641, A1 (Planck 2018 results I), Sect. 5.3

cosmology.name: flat LambdaCDM, Planck 2018 TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO (H0=67.66 km/s/Mpc, Omega_m=0.3111, Omega_Lambda=1-Omega_m, radiation neglected)
cosmology.ref: Planck Collaboration 2020, A&A 641, A6, Table 2 (last column)
cosmology.integration: D_C(z) = (c/H0) * int_0^z dz/sqrt(Om(1+z)^3 + OL); cumulative composite Simpson on a uniform grid dz=1e-5, linear interpolation (error < 1e-6 Mpc); cross-checked against direct Simpson with 2e5 panels

selection.survey: 2MASS Redshift Survey (2MRS) main catalog (Huchra et al. 2012)
selection.skyCoverage: ~91% of the sky: all-sky except the Zone of Avoidance |b|<5 deg, widened to |b|<8 deg for |l|<30 deg (Galactic bulge)

zoneOfAvoidance: No galaxies at |b|<5 deg (|b|<8 deg towards the bulge): renderers will see an empty wedge/disc-shaped gap aligned with the Milky Way plane. This is an observational selection effect (dust extinction and stellar confusion), not a real void.
redshiftSpaceDistortions: Distances are inferred from redshift. Random velocities in clusters stretch them radially ("Fingers of God"); coherent infall flattens large structures (Kaiser effect). The magnitude-limited selection makes the density of points fall with distance (Malmquist-type bias) - do not read the outer thinning as fewer galaxies in reality.

source.catalog: Huchra J.P. et al. 2012, ApJS 199, 26 (2MRS); VizieR J/ApJS/199/26/table3
